issues.legal_issue: A lessor may terminate a lease under a re-entry covenant only when the specified grounds for re-entry are established; ancillary uses that support the educational institution do not establish a detrimental non-educational use.
material_facts: The lease permitted re-entry if the property was used for purposes other than an educational institution or the lessee could no longer manage the institution as an educational institution.
The trial and first appellate courts found no trespass or breach of the covenant.
Shops had been constructed on part of the land, and their rent was used to maintain and run the educational institution.
Some rooms were used for cultural and marriage purposes to augment the society’s funds, without detriment to the running of the institution or the provision of education.
issues.conclusion: The alleged uses did not establish a breach of the lease covenant, and the lessors were not entitled to terminate the lease on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The re-entry covenant applied if the property was used for a purpose other than that for which it was intended, or if the lessee could no longer manage the institution as an educational institution. Ancillary uses that supported the institution and did not detract from its educational purpose did not amount to the specified misuse.

rule.if: lease_termination_dispute and lease_reentry_limited_to_noneducational_use_or_inability and ancillary_uses_support_education and not detrimental_noneducational_use_established

predicates.lease_termination_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a lessor may terminate a lease based on alleged misuse of the leased property.
predicates.lease_reentry_limited_to_noneducational_: The lease permits re-entry only if the property is put to a purpose other than its intended institutional purpose or the lessee can no longer manage the institution for that purpose.
predicates.ancillary_uses_support_education: The lessee uses parts of the property in ancillary ways and applies the resulting income to support the institution.
predicates.detrimental_noneducational_use_establish: The evidence establishes that the property was used for a different purpose in a way that detracts from its intended institutional purpose.

issues.definition: When a lease-termination dispute concerns a re-entry condition limited to non-purpose use or inability to manage the institution, and ancillary uses support the institution without established detrimental non-purpose use, the lessor is not entitled to terminate the lease.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding a second appeal may not reverse concurrent factual findings by reappreciating evidence without a permissible basis for doing so.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court concurrently found no breach of the lease covenant.
In the second appeal, the High Court reappreciated the evidence, found that the property had been allowed to be trespassed and used for other purposes, and decreed the suit.
The Supreme Court held that the High Court had impermissibly revisited the factual findings under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the decrees of the trial court and first appellate court were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not permit a second appellate court to trench upon the appreciation of evidence and reverse concurrent findings of fact in the circumstances presented. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_factual_findings and high_court_reappreciated_evidence and reversed_findings_without_permissible_basis

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding before the reviewing court is a second appeal.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual findings.
predicates.high_court_reappreciated_evidence: The High Court reassessed the evidence in the second appeal.
predicates.reversed_findings_without_permissible_ba: The High Court reversed the concurrent factual findings without a permissible basis for doing so.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, when the High Court reappreciates evidence and reverses concurrent factual findings without a permissible basis, the lower courts’ concurrent decrees are restored.
